title: Buttermilk Panna Cotta with Raspberry Coulis
summary: A light, tangy buttermilk panna cotta, turned out and topped with a bright raspberry coulis.

ingredients.note: about 6 g; check the pack says beef (bovine)

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Bloom
steps.text: sprinkle the gelatine over the cold water in the small bowl and leave 5 min. Soaking first lets the gelatine dissolve without lumps.

steps.title: Warm
steps.text: heat the cream, sugar and salt, stirring, until the sugar dissolves and it is steaming but not boiling. Off the heat, stir in the gelatine until fully melted. Cool 10 min.

steps.title: Add buttermilk
steps.text: whisk in the buttermilk and vanilla; adding it to the cooled cream stops it curdling. Pour into the jug and fill the moulds. Too much heat would split the buttermilk.

steps.title: Set
steps.text: stand the moulds on the tray and chill at least 6 h. A long chill gives a soft, wobbly set.

steps.title: Coulis
steps.text: blend the raspberries, icing sugar and lemon juice and press through the sieve. Sieving removes the seeds for a smooth sauce.

steps.title: Turn out
steps.text: dip each mould in hot water for 5 s, run a knife round the edge and invert onto a plate. Spoon a pool of coulis on top.

tips: A common mistake is boiling the cream once the gelatine is in, which weakens the set; keep it just steaming.
For a softer set, serve it in glasses instead of turning it out.
Make it the day before; it keeps well.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Keep the coulis separately for up to 3 days. Do not freeze.
